title: Tabnas serialized grammar (GrammarSpec)
description: The serialized, pure-JSON form of a Tabnas grammar: the GrammarSpec shape fed to tn.grammar() in TypeScript (ts/src/types.ts GrammarSpec/GrammarAltSpec) and to GrammarSpecFromJSON in Go (go/grammarspec.go). This schema models the PORTABLE JSON form only. The TS-side `ref` property (a map of @-refs to live functions) is deliberately absent: functions are not JSON-serialisable, so a serialized spec cannot carry one — it refers to engine builtins by their $-suffixed FuncRef names (e.g. '@node$') instead, and a caller that needs custom functions supplies a ref bag at load time, outside the serialized document. The Go-only GrammarSpec conveniences (OptionsMap, RuleOrder) are likewise not part of the portable form. Version gate: `v` declares the builtin config-schema version the grammar was compiled against; ABSENT means version 1, and an engine refuses a spec whose `v` exceeds the BUILTIN_SCHEMA_VERSION it implements (ts/src/builtins.ts, go/builtins.go — 3 at the time of writing). That ceiling is deliberately NOT encoded as a maximum here: the schema outlives engine versions, and the refusal is the engine's job.

clear.description: Wipe the instance before applying the rest of this spec: every rule and every fixed-token binding is removed, leaving the lexer matchers (which are not grammar) in place. Both runtimes compare against literal true — a non-boolean is not a clear request.

v.description: Builtin config-schema version this grammar was compiled against. Absent means version 1. The engine refuses a spec whose v exceeds the BUILTIN_SCHEMA_VERSION it implements; no maximum is declared here because that ceiling moves with the engine, not with this schema.

options.description: JSON-serializable options applied before the rules (TabnasOptions). Deliberately free-form: constraining the full TabnasOptions tree is out of scope for this schema. Function-valued option fields use @-prefixed FuncRef strings resolved by the engine.

rule.description: Per-rule alternate definitions, keyed by rule name. A null entry REMOVES that rule from the instance (the declarative form of tn.rule(name, null)); removing a rule that is not there is a no-op.

funcRef.description: A @-prefixed function reference, resolved by the engine: builtin refs end in '$' (e.g. '@node$'); anything else must be supplied in a ref bag at load time.

ruleSpec.description: One rule's alternates, or null to remove the rule.

altsOrList.description: OPEN- or CLOSE-state alternates: either a plain array of alt objects, or an object carrying the alts plus inject operations controlling how they merge into existing alternates.

inject.description: How the alts merge into a rule's existing alternates (default: prepend).

append.description: If true, append; if false or absent, prepend.

clear.description: If true, empty the rule's existing alternates before inserting, so a spec can replace a rule's open/close alternates outright.

delete.description: Indices of existing alternates to delete (negative indices count from the end).

move.description: Pairs of indices: [from, to, from, to, ...].

alt.description: A serialized alternate (TS GrammarAltSpec, ts/src/types.ts; Go GrammarAltSpec, go/grammarspec.go): like AltSpec, but function-valued fields use @-prefixed FuncRef strings.

s.description: Token sequence to match: a string of space-separated token names ('#KEY #CL'), or an array whose elements are per-position alternatives.

b.description: Token push-back count, or a FuncRef computing it.

p.description: Push child rule: a rule name, or a FuncRef computing one.

r.description: Replace with sibling rule: a rule name, or a FuncRef computing one.

a.description: Action(s) on match: a FuncRef, or an array of FuncRefs run in order.

c.description: Match condition: a FuncRef, or a declarative condition object.

n.description: Counter increments, keyed by counter name. Integers are the contract: the TS runtime happens to tolerate floats, but the Go door truncates them (see schema/README.md, known leniencies).

u.description: Custom data attached to the rule.

k.description: Custom data attached to the rule and propagated to child rules.

g.description: Group tags: a comma-separated string or an array of tag strings.
